classification.difficultyReason: Find the radius from the quadrant area, then use it to calculate the quadrant arc length.

content.prompt:
In the circle, the area of the quadrant is $100\text{ cm}^2$.

What is the arc length $l$, correct to one decimal place?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10: circle below the prompt on the left
spec.description: Complete circle centred at O, with diagonal radii enclosing the right-hand quadrant, a derived right-angle marker, its given area, and an external split curved dimension arrow labelled l.
spec.mathematics: The radii meet at 90 degrees. The quadrant area is 100 cm²; l denotes its bounding quarter-circle arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the requested unknown appear in the question diagram. No calculated radius or arc length is shown.

answer.short: $17.7\text{ cm}$. Find $r=\sqrt{\frac{400}{\pi}}\text{ cm}$, then use $l=\frac14(2\pi r)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
A&=\frac{\pi r^2}{4}\\
100&=\frac{\pi r^2}{4}\\
400&=\pi r^2\\
\frac{400}{\pi}&=r^2\\
r&=\sqrt{\frac{400}{\pi}}\text{ cm}\\
l&=\frac14(2\pi r)\\
l&=\frac14\left(2\pi\sqrt{\frac{400}{\pi}}\right)\text{ cm}\\
l&\approx17.7\text{ cm}
\end{align*}$$
